title: Autonomic Nervous System Anatomy: Sympathetic & Enteric
description: Learn autonomic nervous system anatomy, comparing thoracolumbar sympathetic ganglia and splanchnic nerves with craniosacral vagal and pelvic nerve outflow.
h1: Autonomic Nervous System Anatomy: Sympathetic and Parasympathetic
blurb: The involuntary balance between thoracolumbar sympathetic fight-or-flight chains, craniosacral vagal and pelvic parasympathetic rest-and-digest outflow, and gut plexuses.
lead: Operating beneath conscious awareness every second of life, the autonomic nervous system balances heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and pupil size through two complementary divisions. In this illustrated guide to autonomic nervous system anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including sympathetic trunk, chain ganglion, coeliac ganglion & plexus, superior mesenteric ganglion—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Operating beneath conscious awareness every second of life, the autonomic nervous system balances heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and pupil size through two complementary divisions. Deep dive into ganglia and plexuses: where fibres relay, which organs they reach, and what happens when the balance breaks. Within the human body, the autonomic nervous system (Systema nervosum autonomicum) is situated in viscera + vertebral column, receives arterial perfusion via visceral vessels, and is innervated by intrinsic — autonomic.

The sympathetic trunk (Truncus sympathicus) is paired chain from neck to sacrum beside vertebrae. Physiologically, the sympathetic trunk governs mass fight-or-flight discharge. Structurally, the chain ganglion (Ganglion trunci) comprises relay station on the trunk. Physiologically, the chain ganglion governs synapse for pre→postganglionic fibres. Structurally, the coeliac ganglion & plexus (Ganglion coeliacum) comprises largest prevertebral relay at T12/L1, around coeliac trunk. Physiologically, the coeliac ganglion & plexus governs foregut sympathetic supply. Structurally, the superior mesenteric ganglion (Ganglion mesentericum superius) comprises relay at the SMA origin. Physiologically, the superior mesenteric ganglion governs midgut sympathetic supply. Structurally, the inferior mesenteric ganglion (Ganglion mesentericum inferius) comprises relay at IMA origin. Physiologically, the inferior mesenteric ganglion governs hindgut and pelvic sympathetic supply. Structurally, the vagus parasympathetic (N. vagus (parasymp.)) comprises cranial parasympathetic to thorax and fore/midgut. Physiologically, the vagus parasympathetic governs rest-digest: slow heart, stimulate gut.

Clinically, regarding the sympathetic trunk, chronic overdrive: hypertension, anxiety physiology. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the chain ganglion, stellate ganglion block treats refractory angina pain. In clinical pathology involving the coeliac ganglion & plexus, coeliac plexus block for pancreatic cancer pain. Medical evaluation of the superior mesenteric ganglion also notes that mesenteric ischaemia pain is carried with these fibres.

questions.question: What is the difference between sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves?
questions.answer: Both are autonomic pathways. Sympathetic activity often prepares organs for exertion; parasympathetic pathways support many resting functions. Their effects depend on the organ and receptor.

questions.question: Where are autonomic ganglia located?
questions.answer: Sympathetic ganglia lie in chains beside the spine or in prevertebral groups; many parasympathetic ganglia lie near or within their target organs.

questions.question: What is the sympathetic trunk?
questions.answer: The sympathetic trunks are paired chains of ganglia that run alongside the vertebral column from the neck to the sacrum.

questions.question: Where are the coeliac plexus and ganglia located?
questions.answer: The coeliac plexus and ganglia surround the origin of the coeliac trunk, anterior to the aorta near the T12–L1 level.

questions.question: What is the function of the inferior mesenteric ganglion?
questions.answer: The inferior mesenteric ganglion relays sympathetic signals to the hindgut and contributes to pelvic visceral pathways.
